title: Combination of Microstereolithography and Electrospinning to Produce Membranes Equipped with Niches for Corneal Regeneration
protocol: Create L1 by drawing a 1.2 cm black circle using any suitable drawing program.
Include 8 white 0.5 x 0.35 mm horseshoe-shaped structures within the black circle for L2.
Save L1 and L2 in JPEG format.
Mix polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA, Mn = 250 g/mol) with 1% w/w Camphorquinone on a magnetic stirrer for 20 min.
Expand the laser beam using a telescopic lens arrangement.
Project the expanded laser beam onto a computer programmable digital multimirror device (UV-enabled DMD starter kit).
Adjust and carefully clean the optics of the microstereolithography set-up.
Put 300 µl of PEGDA mixture into a well pre-coated with Teflon or other non-stick material in a 12-well tissue culture plate.
Switch on the blue laser (MBL-III 473 nm; 150 mW).
Upload L1 into ALP3-basic software previously installed on the PC.
Irradiate the first layer for 60 seconds.
Add 250 µl more of PEGDA to the well.
Upload L2 as described above and irradiate L2 for 60 seconds.
Remove the uncured polymer from the ring structure.
Wash the ring with isopropanol overnight.
Distribute PEGDA rings on an electroplated aluminum sheet (12 cm x 20 cm) for creating a static electrospinning collector.
Attach the rings using conductive carbon tape.
Prepare PLGA polymer solution by dissolving PLGA in dichloromethane at 20% w/w concentration.
Stir the polymer solution overnight before use.
Load 2.5 ml of PLGA solution into each of four insulin syringes.
Electrospin using a flow rate of 30 µl/min and voltages ranging from 12 to 15 kV.
Maintain a distance of 15 cm between the needles and the collector.
Electrospin for 1 hr and 30 min.
Carefully peel the PLGA electrospun sheet from the collector supporting the PEGDA rings.
Cut the electrospun scaffolds into 22 mm diameter circles using a circular hole punch.
Mount the membrane in a small container (Plastic petri dish) and place it inside a medical grade bag.
Fold filter paper (125 mm diameter) into a semicircle, cut in half, and seal the ends together using tape.
Fill three filter paper bags with 1 g of silica orange, cobalt (II) chloride, and copper (II) sulfate, respectively.
Put the three desiccant bags inside the medical grade bag along with the electrospun membrane.
Add a commercially available six spot humidity indicator card to detect moisture accumulation during storage.
Use a vacuum heat seal machine to vacuum and seal the bag.
Send the ring membranes to an external company for γ-irradiation.
Store γ-irradiated PLGA membranes at temperatures ranging from -20°C to +37°C in a moist environment within an incubator containing 5% CO2.
Examine the humidity indicator after storage to confirm that the level of humidity is below 30%.
Use Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) to assess fiber integrity.
Disinfect rabbit eyes using antiseptic solution (3%).
Clean the eyes by removing excess tissue surrounding the cornea.
Separate the limbal region from the rest of the cornea using a dissection microscope.
Cut the limbal region into segments approximately 1.5 cm long under the dissection microscope.
Disinfect the limbal segments in 1.5% antiseptic solution for 1 min.
Cut the disinfected limbal segments into small pieces (100-500 µm) with a scalpel blade.
Store the small tissue pieces in culture media at 37 °C and 5% CO2 until use, not exceeding 60 min.
Coat ring scaffolds with 15 µl of fibrin glue (1:1 mixture of human plasma fibrinogen at 18.75 mg/ml and thrombin at 2.5 U/ml) using a cell scraper for even distribution.
Place the tissue explants directly on PLGA micropockets using a 25 G needle and dissecting microscope.
Add cell culture media very gently to avoid detaching the explants.
Change media every 3 days using the recipe described in section 3.7.
Maintain cultures for 2 weeks in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Fix samples with 3.7% buffered formaldehyde for 10 min.
Wash fixed samples three times with PBS.
Counterstain by incubating in 1 μg/ml of 4',6-diamidino-2-phenylindole (DAPI) or propidium iodide (PI) for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash stained samples three times with PBS and store covered with foil.
Image samples using a fluorescence microscope at wavelengths of 543 nm and 800 nm.
Clean and disinfect rabbit eyes as described above.
Wound rabbit eyes by immersing them in 0.14% ammonium hydroxide for 5 min.
Rinse wounded eyes in PBS.
Scrape away the epithelium with a sclerotome knife.
Cut and isolate the cornea-scleral button removing any remaining tissue.
Place corneas epithelial side down onto a sterile cup filled with 0.5% agar made in DMEM.
Once set, place corneas epithelial side up in small petri dishes.
Add culture media to the limbal area without covering the whole cornea.
Coat ring membranes with 15 μl of fibrin glue (1:1 mixture of fibrinogen at a concentration of 18.75 mg/ml and thrombin at a concentration of 2.5 U/ml).
Use a cell scraper to apply fibrin glue as described above.
Place the tissue explants directly on the PLGA micropockets using a 25 G needle and a dissecting microscope.
Place the rings with the tissue explants on the denuded corneas with the explants facing up at air-liquid interface conditions.
Maintain the organ culture models for 4 weeks in a humidified incubator at 37 °C and 5% CO2, changing the media every 2 days.
Fix the corneas using 3.7% formaldehyde after 4 weeks.
Process the corneas for conventional histology to produce 6 µm paraffin sections.
Stain the sections with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E).
Dewax the sections in xylene for 3 minutes.
Rehydrate the sections in 100% ethanol for 1 minute, then in 70% ethanol for 1 minute, followed by distilled water for 2 minutes.
Delineate the sections using a Dako pen to delimit small areas and avoid excessive use of antibody.
Treat the delineated areas with 0.05% trypsin (100 µl) for 20 minutes at 37 °C.
Wash the treated areas thoroughly with PBS.
Add 100 µl of 10% goat’s serum for blocking for 1 hour.
Incubate the samples with 100 µl of mouse monoclonal antibody cytokeratin 3 (CK3) and 100 µl of p63 in 1% goat’s serum overnight at 4 °C.
Wash the samples with PBS.
Treat the samples with 100 µl of biotinylated secondary anti-mouse antibody (1:1,000 in 1% goat serum) for 1 hour at room temperature.
Add 100 µl of FITC-streptavidin (1:100 in 1% goat serum) for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Image the samples using a fluorescence microscope at wavelengths of 800 nm (two-photon) and 488 nm.
